title: FFT Bin Calculator
description: With a sample rate of 12,800 Hz and an FFT size of 512, every FFT bin is 12,800 / 512 = 25 Hz wide, and the useful bins run from 0 to 255 (the Nyquist limit of 6,400 Hz would be bin 256). Two formulas cover everything: bin = frequency / 25, and bin center = bin number x 25.
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Open Study Buddy
Signal Processing and the FFT
Frequency Bin
Bin Width
FFT Size
Nyquist Limit

learningObjectives: The learner will calculate the nearest FFT bin for 4 tone frequencies and the center frequency of 2 bins, using a sample rate of 12,800 Hz and an FFT size of 512, with at least 5 of 6 answers correct.
prerequisites: frequency bin, bin width, sample rate, FFT size, Nyquist limit (all defined in this chapter above the block, and in Chapter 3 for sample rate and Nyquist limit).

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Explore, then fixed-order practice items with one attempt each and immediate explained feedback
keyQuestions: Is a tone between two bins lost?
Does a louder tone change the bin width?
Why is there no bin 256 in the useful range?
commonMisconceptions: (1) The bin number equals the frequency in hertz. (2) The bin width depends on the loudness of the tone. (3) A tone between two bins is lost.
assessmentOpportunities: Complete all six challenges. Mastery is 5 of 6 correct on the first attempt.
